transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-03-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Record: yes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Luca Romero (Redwood SE), Sarah Nguyen (CISO, Horizon), Mark Reynolds (Head of Platform, Horizon), Priya Sharma (Security Engineer, Horizon)

Summary:
Quick review of most recent pen test results Redwood ran for Horizon Bank (third-party vendor engagement), discussion on remediation prioritization, vuln mgmt process, secure SDLC integration, and recommended patching cadence. Agreed next steps to share full artifacts and repros.

Topics: SOC 2 relevance, audit logs & retention, RBAC/SSO, KMS/encryption at rest and in-transit, pen test findings (high/medium/low), vuln triage and patching cadence, CI/CD gating for security, timeline for SOC 2 readiness items.

00:00 Sarah: Hi everybody, thanks for joining, we have about 45 minutes, uh, quick round of intros?
00:08 Maya: Hey Sarah, thanks, I'm Maya, account lead for Horizon at Redwood Infrence, that's how the keyboard typed it earlier sorry, and with me is Luca, our security engineer.
00:16 Luca: Hi all, Luca Romero, I focus on infra and vuln repro.
00:19 Mark: Mark Reynolds, Head of Platform, Horizon Bank. Priya is with me, she'll run the follow ups.
00:25 Priya: Hi, Priya Sharma, security engineer.

02:12 Maya: Cool. Quick context, we ran an engagement with a pen test firm last month against the hosted endpoints you have on dedicated pools, we also scanned the private deployment config you asked about — full report's near final, sharing redacted copy. The call today is to walk through top findings, remediation options and how this ties back to SOC 2/ISO controls and your SDLC.

04:00 Luca: I'll start with a show of the findings, there's a handful of high/medium items, one high that is mostly around an outdated dependency used in one of the management UI services (we're seeing an exploitation chain in the scanner results). The CVE is noted as CVE-2025-xxxx in the report.
04:28 Priya: Is that in the hosted control plane or within our VPC?
04:32 Luca: It's in the control plane admin UI that sits in the customer-managed plane for private installs, so Horizon's private deployment surface. For hosted customers it's in the Redwood admin console but isolated. The exploit requires authenticated access plus a crafted payload; the risk is privilege escalation to admin UI functions.

06:10 Sarah: Ok that sounds bad, what's the recommended patch?
06:14 Luca: Upgrade the dependency to 2.x, vendor already has patch, and rotate any service credentials that may have been exposed during the window. We're also recommending a quick fix — WAF rule to block the vector while patch is staged. We can supply the exact rule.

08:05 Mark: For our compliance audit, we need an auditable timeline — when will those creds be rotated and patches applied? Our infra team needs a patch window.
08:16 Maya: We'll put this in the remediation tracker; suggested approach is emergency patch for the high within 72 hours, medium items next sprint (2 weeks). We'll share the tracker with dates.

10:30 Priya: On the medium items there's references to stale TLS cipher config on a sidecar in staging, and some audit logs not retained for long enough per our SOC 2 policy.
10:45 Luca: Right, the audit log retention on a few components defaults to 30 days in the build you shipped; SOC 2 evidence typically expects 90 days plus archival for 1 year depending on control. For the hosted route we can adjust retention and snapshot logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies. For private we provide hooks to forward logs to your SIEM.

13:05 Sarah: That works, we run Splunk so forwarding is fine. Can you confirm logs include token-level request metadata and model id? We need that for forensics.
13:18 Luca: Yes, we capture request metadata including model variant, route id, token counts, latencies; sometimes the auto-transcript OCR mislabels the product names in the report but the raw logs include the fields. We'll give a log schema.

15:40 Mark: On RBAC/SSO, last time you recommended SAML SSO with SCIM for user sync — any outstanding issues?
15:51 Maya: Implementation is stable; for Horizon's private deployment you can tie to your internal IdP and we support role mappings. One note from the pen test: a few service accounts had more privileges than needed — principle of least privilege wasn't enforced for housekeeping jobs.

17:20 Priya: We'll run a role audit. Do you support conditional access for the admin console?
17:26 Luca: We have IP allowlists and SSO enforcement; conditional access like device posture is something we'd integrate via your IdP (Azure AD Conditional Access or Okta). We can provide a runbook.

19:00 Sarah: Encryption at rest and KMS — are keys customer-managed? We need to ensure keys are in our KMS/HSM.
19:09 Maya: Yes, for private deployments you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and integrate with your KMS. For hosted deployments we offer a dedicated KMS integration for enterprise customer-managed key import to HSM is on roadmap but currently we integrate via a dedicated KMS namespace. I'll add the KMS runbook link.

21:35 Priya: Any issues found around data residency or cross-region backups?
21:40 Luca: The pen test didn't flag residency issues, but we did note that backups for a subset of logs were stored in a region different than the primary cluster in one test configuration. We recommend explicit region tags and policy for backup S3 buckets; for SOC 2 you'd want evidence that data never leaves permitted regions.

24:00 Mark: Vulnerability management cadence — what do you recommend? We run weekly scans internally, but want a joint cadence.
24:10 Maya: Proposed: monthly full infra scans by Redwood + quarterly third-party pen test for critical services; immediate critical patching within 72 hours, High within 2 weeks, Medium in 30 days, Low as part of regular release. We can align this with your SLAs.

26:30 Priya: How do we integrate this into our SDLC? We want security gates in CI.
26:38 Luca: We recommend failing merges on high-severity SCA (software composition analysis) findings, have SAST in pipeline for PR checks, and require dependency license and vulnerability scans as gating. We can provide a sample GitHub Actions workflow and a list of baseline checks.

29:00 Sarah: About the repros — can you show an example exploit or logs?
29:08 Luca: Sure, I'll share sanitized repro logs. During the test the exploit chain required an authenticated session; we were able to craft a payload that triggered the vulnerable deserialization in the UI. I'll attach the PoC in the tracker.

31:50 Mark: For our auditors, we need an evidence bundle: pen test report, timeline of remediation, audit log exports, RBAC mapping. Can you produce an attestable package?
32:02 Maya: Yes, we'll assemble a package with the report, remediation spreadsheet, log schema + sample exports, and a SOC 2 mapping doc. We'll redact any PII.

34:10 Priya: On patching cadence, do you handle rolling restarts to avoid downtime on dedicated pools?
34:18 Luca: Yes, we support rolling upgrades with drain and switchover, and you can configure maintenance windows. For critical patches we can enable a faster path but we'll coordinate with your ops.

36:00 Sarah: Are there any outstanding regulatory concerns (ISO 27001 gap) from the test?
36:07 Luca: The report calls out control deficiencies that map to ISO clauses: change management evidence lacks timestamps for one change in the demo env, and the dependency scanning wasn't integrated into the build pipeline for one microservice. Both are remediable; we'll map to controls in the gap analysis.

38:50 Mark: What about alerting — do you integrate with our pager and ticketing?
38:55 Maya: Yes, Redwood can forward security alerts to your PagerDuty and create Jira tickets via webhook. We'll share sample config.

41:10 Priya: Anything else high-risk?
41:15 Luca: Only the one high CVE and a privilege mismatch on a service account; both are actionable. Medium list is mostly config drift and retention. We didn't find evidence of data exfil beyond test accounts.

43:00 Sarah: Ok recap: send full pen test, remediation tracker, log schema, PoC repro logs; set patching SLA and schedule follow-up.
43:12 Maya: Correct. I'll send the pack and set up the follow-up with compliance folks.

44:00 Action Items (verbal):
- Maya to share report + tracker (due 2026-04-01)
- Luca to reproduce PoC on Redwood staging and attach logs (due 2026-04-05)
- Priya to share Horizon patch schedule and vulnerability SLA (due 2026-04-08)

45:12 Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the SOC 2 gap review.
45:20 Sarah: Thanks, appreciate it.
45:30 Call end.
